messages:
maya: Heads-up — we've had a cluster of p99 latency spikes starting ~10:30 UTC. Multiple customers (acme-corp, beta-co) reporting >=3x p99. Initial sign is admission control spiking 429s / long admit delays for tenant=acme-corp.

maya: quick repro (observed from our support test):
```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate\" -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Admit-Delay: 310ms
Retry-After: 5

maya: logs show repeated sem_wait delays and worker pool shrink:
```
[ingress] admit=blocked tenant=acme-corp inflight=1024 max_concurrency=256 sem_wait=310ms workers_alive=0
[autoscaler] scale_decision: replicas->0 reason=failed_liveness_probe
```

arjun: can you paste the k8s events / autoscaler history? workers_alive=0 sounds like the pool got killed.

maya: grabbing events now. repro steps I used to trigger locally:
```bash
# simulate load + flaky readiness
kubectl -n inference exec -it loadgen -- sh -c "while true; do seq 1 100 | xargs -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"input\":\"spam\"}' & done"
# then toggle readinessProbe to fail for 30s
kubectl patch deployment inference-workers -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","readinessProbe":null}]}}}}'
```

dmitri: timeline: around 10:18 we had a noisy liveness probe across us-west-worker-* which triggered HPA downscale; no infra deploy at that time. I've pulled the liveness logs — it looks like a probe race condition when pod restart and graceTimeout overlap.

sofia: impacted customers listed with tickets: ACME-3421, BETA-128. CS has opened P2 cases and informed them we're investigating.

arjun: immediate mitigations I recommend:
- bump tenant admission soft limit for acme-corp from 256->512 for 15m via runtime config
- enable fallback routing for that tenant to the lightweight model variant (lower cost, lower mem)
- return Retry-After headers so clients backoff (we already do, but ensure value is 5s)
- add a temporary rule to prefer nodes with available workers (route-policy=prefer-healthy)

arjun: example runtime patch (canary):
```json
{
  "tenant":"acme-corp",
  "admit":{ "soft_limit":512, "retry_after":5 },
  "routing":{ "fallback_model":"gpt-small-v2" }
}
```

maya: I'm going to apply the canary config to us-west-canary-3 now, and enable prefer-healthy routing. Will monitor p95/p99 dashboards.

ops-bot: Deployment started: config/tenants/acme-corp -> canary/us-west-canary-3 by maya (action: apply)

dmitri: I'll push the probe-flap hotfix patch to node-probes branch and roll to worker autoscaler. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/1234 (hotfix: extend liveness grace and fix race).

lucy: I'll coordinate a rolling restart of the affected worker pool after canary is green. Also updating the public status page and adding a note for impacted customers.

support-lead: Please confirm ETA for CS update so we can message customers.

maya: Mitigation ETA: config canary applied in ~2m, expect p99 -> baseline in 5-10m if routing paths pick up. Full fix (probe hotfix + controlled restart) ~2 hours. I'll post metrics when p95/p99 drop. :thumbsup:

arjun: If canary doesn't help, plan B: temporarily redirect 20% of acme traffic to backup region and enable conservative admission (max_concurrency=128) to keep tail bounded.

maya: noted. Monitoring: dashboard link -> https://dashboards.redwood.dev/d/ingress/tenant-p99?orgId=1&tenant=acme-corp (watching p95/p99, admit queue length).

support-lead: thanks — will inform CS and escalate if SLA risk grows.

maya: updating this thread as we see changes. Current: canary applied, p95 dropped 30%, p99 still elevated but trending down.

ops-bot: Deployment succeeded: config/tenants/acme-corp -> canary/us-west-canary-3 (duration 00:01:42)

dmitri: rolling hotfix to autoscaler now. Will coordinate restart window to avoid simultaneous downscale.

lucy: scheduling restart in 15m, will drain connections gracefully first.

maya: final note: please add a regression test for autoscaler when readiness toggles under pressure — we should prevent scale-to-zero when inflight > 0.

sofia: added to product/ops backlog.

maya: thanks all.
